question.p: 2293. Deputy Louis O'Hara asked the Minister for Rural and Community Development and the Gaeltacht if his Department administers any funding schemes which can support provision of Christmas lights in rural towns and villages; and if he will make a statement on the matter. [19548/26]

speech.from: Minister for Rural and Community Development and the Gaeltacht
speech.p: In line with policy commitments in Our Rural Future and Town Centre First, my Department implements a range of capital investment schemes which support the regeneration of our rural towns and villages. In recent years, there has been unprecedented growth in the funding available for such schemes, with projects of varied scale and focus being allocated funding in rural communities all across the country. Within the broad range of support available for projects, the schemes most relevant to the Deputy's particular request are set out below. The Local Enhancement Programme (LEP) provides small grants to community groups to enhance their facilities. Funding of €7 million is provided under the LEP 2026 to support small capital works projects. The programme supports festival lighting including Christmas lights. In general, support under the LEP is available to, for example, Parish Halls, Community Centres, Local Development Associations, Social Clubs, Senior Citizen Groups, Men’s and Women’s Sheds. The LEP is administered locally on behalf of the Department by Local Community Development Committees (LCDCs) across the country, with support from their Local Authority. Groups apply directly to the relevant LCDC, who then appraise the applications and provide a list to the Department. Once the approved projects fall within the ethos of the fund the Department entrusts the LCDCs to make decisions on their eligibility. This allows for autonomy under the fund and also ensures that groups most in need received funding. The Town and Village Renewal Scheme (TVRS) is administered through local authorities and designed to rejuvenate rural towns and villages throughout Ireland. Delivered in partnership with local authorities, it primarily targets funding at areas with populations of less than 10,000 people. Over €210 million has been allocated to over 1,900 projects since the launch of the scheme in 2016. I announced the most recent round of funding under the 2025 Town and Village Renewal Scheme last December, and that scheme placed a renewed focus on town centre economic and social recovery and regeneration. The provision of festival lighting including Christmas lights may be supported as part of an application under the scheme. The LEADER Programme provides support to rural communities under a broad range of themes, including Rural Infrastructure and Social Inclusion. LEADER has for many years supported community projects, including the purchase of Christmas lights, once they are compatible with the Operating Rules and the Local Development Strategy for the relevant LEADER area. LEADER projects are selected and approved by the Local Action Group, and the Department has no role in approving projects. Prospective applicants should, in the first instance, contact their relevant LAG, through its Implementing Partner to discuss the eligibility of the project and the funding that may be available. Further information is available on [www.gov.ie/LEADER].

question.p: 2294. Deputy Shane Moynihan asked the Minister for Rural and Community Development and the Gaeltacht the person or body with responsibility for the TidyTowns programme, including oversight and administration; and if he will make a statement on the matter. [19573/26]

speech.from: Minister for Rural and Community Development and the Gaeltacht
speech.p: The SuperValu TidyTowns annual competition is a nationwide initiative that encourages communities to enhance the appearance and sustainability of their local areas. It is a unique volunteer-led programme that makes a hugely positive contribution in communities across Ireland. The Tidy Towns unit of my Department administers the Tidy Towns competition in conjunction with the long-time sponsors, SuperValu. The Tidy Towns unit is based within the Rural Regeneration unit of the Department . I understand that officials from the Tidy Towns unit have also engaged directly with the Deputy's office in respect of the administrative structures underpinning the programme.

question.p: 2295. Deputy Albert Dolan asked the Minister for Rural and Community Development and the Gaeltacht the supports currently available to connected hubs to assist with the employment of hub managers; whether funding is available specifically towards salary and operational costs; the criteria that applies; and the process by which hubs may apply for such supports. [19623/26]

speech.from: Minister for Rural and Community Development and the Gaeltacht
speech.p: Our Rural Future, the Government's Rural Development Policy, recognises the importance of remote working for rural regeneration and committed to establishing a comprehensive and integrated national network of 400 remote working hubs by the end of 2025. I was delighted to announce at the National Hub Summit last November that we have reached that key target, and there are now over 400 hubs on-boarded to the Connected Hubs platform.

At the centre of the commitment to deliver the network of 400 hubs is the connectedhubs.ie online platform which provides hub owners and customers with a central, easy to use portal that offers and enables the booking and payment for a range of services, particularly professional remote working spaces and meeting rooms. The platform is funded by my Department and managed by the Western Development Commission.

The platform provides visibility for each hub to promote its services and facilities on a national platform and presents a common location where users can identify where remote working hubs are located and what facilities are available. Remote working facilities can be booked and paid for on the platform, thus greatly simplifying the payment process, particularly for community run hubs.

Across the Connected Hubs network, there is a range of ownership models in place with some run as privately owned businesses, some are owned and operated by local community groups, while others are managed by local authorities. These hubs and hub managers benefit from a range of supports delivered by the Connected Hubs team in the WDC through network events and collaboration such as shared learning, peer learning and training supports, collective marketing and strategic partnerships with providers for the delivery of services within hubs (for example, Learning in the Hubs was launched in conjunction with the Technology University of the Shannon in 2023).

While my Department does not have a scheme specifically for the employment of hub managers or operational costs, the Community Services Programme (CSP) supports community organisations to provide social, economic and environmental services, including remote working facilities, through a social enterprise model where private sector services are lacking. The CSP Programme provides an annual co-funding contribution towards each full-time equivalent position being supported and, where warranted, towards the cost of employing a manager. The CSP contribution is not aligned to the minimum wage and is not intended to meet the full salary cost of supported posts. In December last year I announced, with my colleague Minister Buttimer, our intention to hold an open call in early 2026 for new organisations to join the CSP Programme as set out in the Programme for Government commitments. The design of this open call is underway and details, including eligible services and organisations, is expected to be announced in the coming weeks.

My department has invested significantly in the establishment and development of remote working facilities through the range of schemes which make up my Department's Rural Development Investment Programme. Funding will continue to form part of capital schemes such as the Rural Regeneration and Development Scheme (RRDF) and the Town and Village Renewal Scheme (TVRS). Since 2020, over 200 remote working facilities have been supported by these schemes.

My department has also implemented targeted schemes to support hubs on the network. For example, the Connected Hubs Calls were introduced in 2021 and 2022 to support the development of facilities in remote working hubs across Ireland. These calls funded additional desk spaces and improved related services, such as privacy booths, technical equipment, meeting facilities and access controls. Almost €14 million was allocated across 200 projects under these schemes. Similarly, the Programme for Government commits to the implementation of a further phase of the Connected Hubs Voucher Scheme which was introduced in 2022 as a further support for hubs on the network.

In addition, to ensure that we can build on the progress achieved in establishing the Connected Hubs network to date, I intend to publish the first National Hubs Strategy shortly. The strategy is being developed jointly with the Department of Enterprise, Tourism and Strategy, and will present a coherent approach to the future development of remote working hubs. I am committed to ensuring that remote working infrastructure can continue to deliver real benefits for rural communities across the country.

question.p: 2296. Deputy Carol Nolan asked the Minister for Rural and Community Development and the Gaeltacht if the provision of panic alarms for elderly people will still remain under the remit of his Department; if it will continue to be managed by Pobal in collaboration with Age Friendly Ireland who take applications from elderly people; and if he will make a statement on the matter. [19954/26]

speech.from: Minister of State at the Department of Rural and Community Development and the Gaeltacht
speech.p: My Department is responsible for the Seniors Alert Scheme which encourages community support for older people in our communities through the provision of personal monitored alarms to enable them to live securely in their homes with confidence, independence and peace of mind. Funding is available under the scheme towards the purchase, by a registered community-based organisation, of a personal alarm or pendant and one year of monitoring. The scheme has an allocation of €3.2million in 2026, with additional support from the 2026 Dormant Accounts Fund. Since the scheme was launched in 2015, 159,090 participants have been approved for the alarms, including over 17,738 in 2025. My Department is currently reviewing all aspects of the Seniors Alert Scheme, including the technology and services available, and I hope to launch of a new iteration of the scheme in 2026. I am continuing to engage with stakeholders including Pobal and Age Friendly Ireland in relation to the next iteration. There is no plan at present to transfer responsibility for the Seniors Alert Scheme to another Government department.

question.p: 2297. Deputy Paul Lawless asked the Minister for Rural and Community Development and the Gaeltacht if his Department has engaged with a commercial service provider (details supplied) regarding their inability to correctly record Irish names containing síneadh fada characters; whether this practice is consistent with State expectations for companies operating in Gaeltacht areas and throughout the State; and if he will make a statement on the matter. [19966/26]

2298. Deputy Paul Lawless asked the Minister for Rural and Community Development and the Gaeltacht if he will request from a company (details supplied) the total number and percentage of its customers residing in Gaeltacht regions and in the West of Ireland; and the steps his Department will take to ensure that companies providing essential services in these areas meet minimum Irish language accommodation standards. [19967/26]

2299. Deputy Paul Lawless asked the Minister for Rural and Community Development and the Gaeltacht his Department's position on telecommunications and broadband companies operating in the State without an Irish language strategy, despite providing essential services in Gaeltacht communities; and whether he intends to raise with a company (details supplied) their reported lack of any policy for enabling Irish speaking customers to communicate with their support teams. [19968/26]

2300. Deputy Paul Lawless asked the Minister for Rural and Community Development and the Gaeltacht if he considers the failure of major service providers to support Irish language name formatting and customer service pathways to be compatible with the goals of the National Plan for Irish Language Public Services 2024-2030; and the measures that are available to his Department to promote compliance with this plan among private commercial entities. [19969/26]

speech.from: Minister for Rural and Community Development and the Gaeltacht
speech.p: I propose to take Questions Nos. 2297, 2298, 2299 and 2300 together.

The Deputy should be aware that both the provisions contained in the Official Languages Acts 2003 to 2021 and the actions contained in the Action Plan for Irish-medium Public Services 2026-2028 are directed at public sector organisations rather than private sector commercial entities.

While my Department has had no contact with the company referred to by the Deputy, in view of the importance of the commercial sector as regards the promotion and visibility of the language, both my own Department and its language agencies, Foras na Gaeilge and Údarás na Gaeltachta, support a number of initiative aimed at promoting the use of the language among the business community. My Department's Scéimeanna Tacaíochta Gaeilge provides support for the use of Irish in the business community through a variety of initiatives, including GRADAIM, a recognition scheme for businesses either using Irish directly as part of their operations or providing a service through Irish to their customers. The awards are presented to businesses for their efforts in three main categories, namely Signage, Branding and Marketing and Irish Language Customer & Client Service. Over 330 businesses have received recognition under this scheme so far. The scheme is administered by Glór na nGael who are the lead Irish language organisation with responsibilities to promote the Irish language in business. In addition to this, my Department provides funding to organisations such as Gnó Mhaigh Eo, Gaillimh le Gaeilge, Baile Átha Cliath le Gaeilge and Cill Dara le Gaeilge, to support and encourage businesses in the use of Irish. Foras na Gaeilge, through its ‘Gnó Means Business’ programme, deliver a wide range of initiatives to support the use of the Irish language in business and economic life, including:

• a funding support scheme focused on small and medium enterprises: Under this scheme, funding of up to €3,000 is available to support the development of signage, stationery, printed marketing material, internet sites and other branding material in the Irish language or bilingually;

• a Business Support Resource Pack: Under this scheme, there are 31 specialist business support resources available free of charge. As part of the support package, there is a choice of self-adhesive signs, badges, leaflets and other support resources to enhance the visibility of Irish in a business environment;

Bilingual Packaging: A Guide for Best Business Practice• is the second in a series of guidance ebooks published by Foras na Gaeilge for the business sector focusing on the principles of bilingualism in signage and packaging. The guidebook aims to recognise best practice in the use of Irish in packaging and to demonstrate to the business community that the language is a valuable resource that can be used to attract consumers to their products. This ebook, which is a joint venture between Foras na Gaeilge and TU Dublin, was launched in 2017 and is available to download from the Foras na Gaeilge website [www.forasnagaeilge.ie].

• Q-Mharc Gnó le Gaeilge is a voluntary code and newly-developed quality system for the Business Sector which focuses on giving official recognition to best bilingual practice based on the International Standard ISO 9001:2008. Small and medium sized enterprises throughout the island of Ireland can apply for this award.

As regards Údarás na Gaeltachta, 2026 will see the roll-out of two new schemes by the organisation aimed at increasing the use of Irish among the business community in the Gaeltacht. The first of these will be targeted at the organisation's network of client companies with a view to introducing the concept of language planning to companies' operations and practices, while the second will be targeted at small retailers and service providers across the Gaeltacht with a view to providing services to customers through the medium of Irish. It is my view that these new schemes, in tandem with the excellent work being carried out by the network of Language Planning Officers in the 26 Gaeltacht Language Planning Areas, will have a positive impact on the use and visibility of the language among Gaeltacht communities.

question.p: 2301. Deputy Sorca Clarke asked the Minister for Rural and Community Development and the Gaeltacht the number of WTE qualified accountants working within his Department as of 10 March 2026, in tabular form. [20027/26]

speech.from: Minister for Rural and Community Development and the Gaeltacht

speech.from: Minister for Rural and Community Development and the Gaeltacht
speech.p: I can confirm that my Department has not had any staff at these grades transfer to another Department or public body during their probationary period in the past five years. Staff are not eligible to transfer to another Department within two years of joining the Civil Service, and so are not eligible to transfer during their probationary period.

question.p: 2308. Deputy Niamh Smyth asked the Minister for Rural and Community Development and the Gaeltacht to review correspondence (details supplied); if he will assist with the query by way of advice; and if he will make a statement on the matter. [20594/26]

speech.from: Minister of State at the Department of Rural and Community Development and the Gaeltacht
speech.p: The Charities Regulator, under the aegis of my Department, is the statutory body responsible for registering and regulating all of Ireland’s charities, with a mandate to promote good governance practice. While the Regulator is under the aegis of my Department, it is fully independent in the performance of its statutory functions. The correspondence referred to was reviewed by officials in my department when received and a response will issue to the Deputy shortly. The Regulator must adhere to the Charities Acts when making decisions and as such must take due care and time with their work. Notwithstanding this, the Regulator deals with all applications in chronological order and strives to issue decisions in as short a timeframe as possible. However, timelines for decision-making can be impacted by factors beyond the control of the Regulator, such as delays on the part of applicants or their agents in responding to queries from the Regulator.

question.p: 2313. Deputy John Connolly asked the Minister for Rural and Community Development and the Gaeltacht the position regarding the Inis Oírr Pier Redevelopment project; the progress made to date; the forthcoming stages of the project lifecycle and the expected timelines for their completion; and the estimated cost range for the project; and if he will make a statement on the matter. [20673/26]

speech.from: Minister for Rural and Community Development and the Gaeltacht
speech.p: Galway County Council is responsible for the maintenance and development of piers on Oileáin Árann, including Inis Oírr. In August 2025 I approved an allocation of €35 million to Galway County Council for the Inis Oírr pier development, the first project announced under the revised National Development Plan. Galway County Council appointed the principal contractor, Ward & Burke last autumn after a competitive tendering process, with a value of over €30 million on the construction contract. The project is expected to be completed within two years. To date, the contractor has carried out preliminary works, such as physical modelling and establishing the site compound on the island. As part of the preparation works on the island, I am advised that a new pedestrian footpath has been constructed adjacent to the primary school to enhance safe access for the duration of the works and beyond. I understand work has very recently started on the island itself with full operations scheduled to start at the end of March. The contractor also held a community information meeting on the island on 19 February to keep residents up to date of the plans. My Department has established a project steering group with Galway County Council for the duration of the project, whereby monthly progress updates are provided to allow for full oversight of the project development and expenditure.

question.p: 2314. Deputy John Connolly asked the Minister for Rural and Community Development and the Gaeltacht the position regarding the Ionad Oideachais agus Óige Indreabhán; the progress made to date; the forthcoming stages of the project lifecycle and the expected timelines for completion; and the estimated cost range for the project; and if he will make a statement on the matter. [20674/26]

speech.from: Minister for Rural and Community Development and the Gaeltacht
speech.p: The development, in conjunction with Údarás na Gaeltachta, of the Ionad Oideachais agus Óige in Indreabhán is one of my Department’s strategic priorities under the National Development Plan. The aim of this project is to build a modern, multi-purpose facility to replace the existing Údarás-owned building currently used by Coláiste Lurgan. The new facility, which is designed for year-round use, will be operated by Údarás na Gaeltachta outside the summer season as an education, youth and community facility for use by the community and will support Coláiste Lurgan’s summer college programme during the summer months. A Grant of €314,280 was awarded by my Department on 12/06/2023 for the design stage of the project including professional services, preparation of a planning application and the preparation and issuing of tender documents. Planning Permission was obtained for the project in 2024. Tender documents were issued on the eTenders platform on 06/02/2026 for the procurement of a contractor to undertake the construction stage of the development. The deadline for receipt of tenders is 27/03/26. The cost of the construction stage of the project is estimated at circa €9,000,000. A detailed timeline for the next stages cannot be provided until the completion of the tendering process. However, it is expected to have the new facility operational in 2028.

question.p: 2315. Deputy John Connolly asked the Minister for Rural and Community Development and the Gaeltacht the position regarding the Islands Minor Capital Works Programme in Galway West constituency; the progress made under the programme; the forthcoming phases and expected timelines for delivery; and the estimated cost range associated with the programme; and if he will make a statement on the matter. [20675/26]

speech.from: Minister for Rural and Community Development and the Gaeltacht
speech.p: My Department’s dedicated capital funding allocation for the islands is aimed primarily at supporting the development of infrastructure serving our islands. Each year, my Department provides capital funding to support local authorities in delivering infrastructure projects and minor capital works on islands and mainland piers and airstrips serving the islands. Earlier this year, my Department invited the relevant local authorities, including Galway County Council, to submit proposals for the 2026 Minor Works Programme. The deadline for receipt of proposals was 27th February 2026. Applications under the programme have been received by the Department from a number of local authorities, including Galway County Council, and are currently being assessed. The funding to be allocated to any local authority depends on the scale of proposals submitted and assessed to be suitable. It is expected that allocations will be approved in early summer to enable works to be completed by the end of September.
